name: Nexkin Adaptive Undershirt
description:
A form-fitting crew-neck undershirt from Nexkin — a Tier 3/4 technical apparel label — made from a proprietary stretch-weave fabric embedded with a passive thermal regulation mesh. The mesh doesn't require power; it's a phase-change material woven directly into the fabric that absorbs heat when the wearer runs hot and releases it when they cool down. The effect is subtle and real: not air conditioning, not heating, just a persistent effort to keep the wearer somewhere near comfortable. The shirt itself is seamless at the shoulders and sides, with flat-locked seams everywhere else.

It's designed to be worn under other garments and is almost aggressively uninteresting to look at — available in black, white, and a medium grey. The value is entirely in the wear. Tier 3 office workers, people with augments that run hot, and anyone who spends long hours in climate-inconsistent environments (construction, field work, transit) wear these as a quiet investment in their own comfort. Some Tier 4 professionals wear them under suits without mentioning it.
functionality: Passive thermal regulation via phase-change material mesh — no power required. Absorbs excess body heat and releases it gradually to maintain consistent skin-surface temperature. Effective range approximately ±4°C from baseline comfort.
what_it_says: You've solved problems other people don't bother to think about. Practical investment in invisible comfort — the kind of person who optimizes without making a show of it.
worn_by: office workers with augments that run hot
story_hooks: A batch of Nexkin undershirts from late 2199 has a phase-change material that was slightly overformulated — under extreme stress conditions (high-intensity physical exertion in hot environments), the mesh can release heat too quickly, causing localized surface burns.
Someone has been stealing Nexkin undershirts specifically — not for resale, but apparently for the phase-change material itself, which has an unrelated industrial application someone has figured out.
A character's Nexkin undershirt malfunctions during a high-stakes situation, its thermal regulation kicking in at exactly the wrong moment and masking a fever they needed to be aware of.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist crew-neck undershirt that hugs the torso with athletic precision. The seamless construction creates an almost second-skin appearance—no bulk, no visual noise. Designed to disappear under layers rather than command attention.
physical_description.fit: Form-fitting but not restrictive; compression-adjacent without the aggressive squeeze. Follows the natural contours of the body with gentle stretch. Shoulders sit flush; torso tapers slightly at the sides.
physical_description.primary_material: Proprietary stretch-weave synthetic blend with embedded passive thermal phase-change mesh. Feels like high-quality athletic knit but with subtle technical weight.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost silky to the touch with an imperceptible ribbed micro-pattern from the phase-change mesh integration. No visible texture variation—the tech is invisible to the eye but present to the skin.
physical_description.color_scheme: Offered in utilitarian black, clean white, and neutral medium grey. No branding visible; no patterns or accents. Absolute chromatic restraint.
physical_description.closures: None—designed as a pullover crew-neck with no zippers, buttons, or fasteners. Fits and functions as a base layer.
distinctive_features: Seamless shoulder and side construction for zero chafe
Flat-locked seams throughout for durability and comfort
Invisible phase-change thermal mesh woven into fabric
Zero visible branding or logos—unmarked technical wear
Minimal visual footprint—designed to work under other garments
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3/4 functional wear. Affordable enough for working-class adoption but engineered with corpo-grade materials. Signals practical investment rather than conspicuous consumption.
physical_description.cultural_context: The wearer prioritizes function over aesthetics. Worn by field technicians, augment-heavy individuals managing thermal load, office workers seeking quiet comfort optimization, and professionals who value invisible performance. It's the uniform of people who've learned that comfort is infrastructure.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new; develops a soft, broken-in patina with regular wear. Holds shape exceptionally well. No visible degradation from thermal cycling. After months of use, appears almost identical to new—a feature, not a bug.
